title: Historic former family home to come under paranormal scrutiny on Halloween
excerpt: A paranormal investigation is happening at Carrow House in King Street on Halloween. Shadow Hunters UK is hoping to identify ghosts in the cellars.
content:
Paranormal investigators are returning to a Victorian house in Norwich to identify the ghosts that many believe haunt its cellars.

Sam Howett, Angel-Mae Howett, Darren Gowing and Wayne Yaxley are scoping out Carrow House for the second time with 20 guests on October 31.

Carrow House (Image: Submitted)

The group, known as Shadow Hunters UK, were met with "shuffling footsteps" and "muffled voices" when exploring the site with ghost-hunting equipment, including cat balls and REM pods, in May.

And this time round they are hoping to find out exactly who the spirits are that roam in the cellars of the 19th century site.

Beneath the house are cellars (Image: Submitted)

Inside one of the cellars (Image: Submitted)

Ms Howett said: "This is the biggest site we have been to.

"It is so vast you have three levels you can investigate.

"I've never been anywhere before where you get that feeling in those cellars.

"I am slightly nervous to go back.

During the visit in May (Image: Submitted)

"We plan to use an infinity deck during our investigation."

An infinity deck is a set of cards used by some paranormal investigators who believe it can help them communicate with spirits or receive answers to questions.

"We also have cameras that we can set up to capture any anomalies while we are elsewhere in the building," she added.

Ms Howett added in one of the glass panels of the building there is an "intriguing" Colman family motto which reads 'soon enough if well enough'.

The building is grade II listed (Image: Submitted)

The site in King Street (Image: Submitted)

Carrow House is known for its connection to the Colman family and the mustard industry.

The event is in collaboration with Norwich Unity Hub CIO, a charity that hires out the site to community organisations.

Sarah King, from the charity, said: "While we'll leave it to visitors to decide what's lurking in the cellars, we're always delighted to welcome people who want to experience this unique building for themselves.

"The investigations have proved extremely popular and the income generated helps Norwich Unity Hub continue supporting charities, community groups and social enterprises across Norfolk."
